title: adidas Kiosk
subtitle: Friends & Family Kiosk at Fashion Week
meta_description: The Rezet Store × adidas Originals Friends & Family Kiosk: a Fashion Week activation with custom sodas, ice cream and T-shirt printing, developed by Sarah Al-farhan from concept to execution.
card_intro: An open meeting point during Fashion Week, with custom sodas, ice cream and T-shirt printing. Developed from concept to execution.
provenance: A project from Sarah Al-farhan’s portfolio, created during her time as Brand and Community Manager at Rezet Store.
intro: With everyone constantly on the move during Fashion Week, the idea was a space where people could stop, recharge and enjoy something refreshing. The Friends & Family Kiosk turned Rezet Store into an open, welcoming meeting point: part break, part brand experience.
facts: Brand and Community Manager, Rezet Store

lead.alt: The Friends & Family Kiosk inside Rezet Store: a black counter with white adidas stripes, menu boards and walls of sneakers behind it.

quote.text: My idea was to create something different: an activation that felt authentic to our community while also offering something genuinely valuable to the consumer.

context: Fashion Week is full of people on the move. The kiosk gave them a reason to slow down: an open and welcoming environment where everyone felt invited to come by, connect and take a break from the busy pace.
The aim was a playful, accessible space that felt as much like an experience as it did a place to take a break.
role: Sarah developed the entire kiosk experience from concept to execution: shaping the initial idea, designing the space, creating custom sodas and ice creams, developing custom T-shirt printing and bringing all of the visual details together.
execution: Concept for an open Friends & Family Kiosk during Fashion Week
Space design: a black counter with white stripes, finished like an oversized shoebox with its own Rezet Store label
Custom sodas and ice creams, alongside a coffee menu
Custom T-shirt printing: Rezet Store × adidas Originals Kiosk tees
Visual details throughout, from menu boards to packaging

gallery.caption: The counter as an oversized shoebox, complete with a Friends & Family Kiosk label.

title: Rezet Lookbook
subtitle: Lookbook, Autumn Winter 2025
meta_description: The Rezet Store Lookbook Autumn Winter 2025: a store lookbook approached as a magazine, showing brands, products and styling through an editorial, fashion-driven lens.
card_intro: A lookbook approached as a magazine: Rezet Store’s brands, products and styling seen through a more editorial, fashion-driven lens.
provenance: A project from Sarah Al-farhan’s portfolio, created during her time as Brand and Community Manager at Rezet Store.
intro: The idea was to create a lookbook showcasing the diverse range of brands available at Rezet Store, while presenting them through a more elevated and fashion-driven lens.
facts: Brand and Community Manager, Rezet Store

lead.alt: Cover of the Rezet Store Lookbook Autumn Winter 2025: a model in a black track jacket and a long grey skirt against an olive background.

quote.text: I wanted to approach the lookbook as a magazine: something visually engaging, inspirational, and relevant to our community.

context: Rather than a product overview, the lookbook was designed to live beyond the store: a piece of content that could be used across different platforms and inspire people to see Rezet Store from a different perspective.
By highlighting brands, products and styling in a more editorial way, it shows not only what the store had to offer, but how it could be worn, combined and interpreted.
role: Sarah shaped the idea and the editorial approach: treating the lookbook as a magazine and presenting the store’s brands through a fashion-driven lens.
execution: Magazine format, with a cover and editorial spreads
A selection across the diverse range of brands at Rezet Store
Styling that shows how pieces can be worn, combined and interpreted
Content made to work across different platforms

gallery.alt: An open spread from the Rezet Store Lookbook showing two styled looks against an olive background.
gallery.caption: An editorial spread from the Autumn Winter 2025 lookbook.

title: adidas Ways to Style
subtitle: Adistar Control 5
meta_description: Ways to Style: an adidas series exploring the Adistar Control 5 through Hashim Musa, Mohammed Chahrour and Elshan Baku in Copenhagen. Individuality, movement and self-expression.
card_intro: A series exploring the versatility of the Adistar Control 5 through the people who wear it: individuality in motion, in Copenhagen.
provenance: A project from Sarah Al-farhan’s portfolio.
intro: Ways to Style is a series exploring the versatility of the Adistar Control 5 through the people who wear them. Each story captures individuality in motion, showing how footwear becomes an extension of self-expression in everyday life.
facts: Hashim Musa, Mohammed Chahrour, Elshan Baku

lead.alt: A man in a black puffer jacket, white T-shirt and red trousers stands by a building entrance, wearing silver Adistar Control 5 sneakers.

quote.text: An ode to the creatives of the city and to those who live in constant motion.

context: This edition takes place in Copenhagen, in the world of Hashim Musa, Mohammed Chahrour and Elshan Baku. Here, sneakers are more than just style: they are movement, rhythm and identity.
From each of their creative workspaces to the city streets, the Adistar Control 5 moves with them, adapting to every moment.
role: Ways to Style is part of Sarah Al-farhan’s portfolio. Details of her role and the full production credits are available on request.
execution: Three Copenhagen creatives: Hashim Musa, Mohammed Chahrour and Elshan Baku
Stories that move from their creative workspaces to the city streets
The Adistar Control 5 styled in everyday life, from the bike to the pavement
Short, social-first stories built around individuality and movement

title: Timberland × Rezet
subtitle: A Fashion Week day of talk, drinks and customization
partners: Rezet Store × Timberland, with Pablo T-Shirt Factory
meta_description: Timberland × Rezet at Copenhagen Fashion Week: a breakfast panel talk at Rezet Store and an evening of live laser-print customization at Pablo T-Shirt Factory, created and produced by Sarah Al-farhan.
card_intro: A Copenhagen Fashion Week day that moved from a breakfast panel at Rezet Store to live laser-print customization at Pablo T-Shirt Factory.
provenance: A project from Sarah Al-farhan’s portfolio, created during her time as Brand and Community Manager at Rezet Store.
intro: For Copenhagen Fashion Week, Sarah created and produced an event with Timberland and Rezet Store, bringing together a morning panel talk, drinks, customization and an evening experience with Pablo T-Shirt Factory.
facts: Timberland, Rezet Store, Pablo T-Shirt Factory
Brand and Community Manager, Rezet Store

lead.alt: Group photo inside Rezet Store after the Timberland breakfast panel talk, with Timberland boots on the shelves behind.

programme.text: Breakfast and a panel talk on creativity, culture and the future of fashion, with Mads Damind, Sallys Sneakers and Darron McKoy, Timberland’s VP of Product Design & Creative Direction.
A live laser-print customization experience with Pablo T-Shirt Factory, where the day’s conversation became something hands-on.

quote.text: Guests were able to engage directly with the craft and create something personal, turning the event from a conversation into an interactive experience.

context: The day brought together voices from across the creative and fashion communities, and then moved from conversation to making: from a panel at Rezet Store in the morning to hands-on customization in the evening.
role: Sarah was responsible for bringing the different elements together: the event concept and programming, the collaboration with Timberland and Pablo T-Shirt Factory, the panel, drinks, guest experience and the transition from the daytime talk into the evening activation.

title: Nike Event Consulting
subtitle: Guest management, seeding and event project management
meta_description: Event consulting for Nike: guest lists, invitations, product seeding, relationship management and on-the-ground coordination of events and brand activations by Sarah Al-farhan.
card_intro: Consulting on Nike events and brand activations: guest lists, invitations, product seeding, relationships and on-the-ground coordination.
provenance: A project from Sarah Al-farhan’s portfolio, from her work as a consultant for Nike.
intro: As a consultant for Nike, Sarah supported the planning and execution of events and brand activations, with a focus on guest management, seeding and overall event project management.
facts: Consultant: guest management, seeding, event project management

lead.alt: Guests gather under a skylight in a white Nike activation space with a large black Swoosh on the wall.

quote.text: The work combined strategy, project management, community building, and cultural engagement.

context: An activation depends on who is in the room. The work focused on ensuring the right mix of creatives, athletes, industry voices and cultural figures were engaged with the brand, and on creating relevant touchpoints between Nike and its community.
role: Sarah developed and managed guest lists, coordinated invitations and attendance, and worked on product seeding and relationship management. She also supported the wider event process: stakeholders, timelines, logistics and on-the-ground execution.
execution: Developing and managing guest lists
Coordinating invitations and attendance
